- [S1626] types=[CORRECTION, FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Splits the prior single Valid(K) (S1612) into 4 explicit predicates: StructuralValid (now with acyclicity of all 3 DAG relations added as a 4th conjunct, per S1624), SemanticallyValid (adding WellFormed(P) per Q14, available only since CB-2 closed via S1622), EpistemicallyValid (recorded-not-absent contradiction -- a knowledge base MAY legitimately hold conflict), and GovernanceValid (not a property of K alone, requires History) -- only the first two are computable from K alone." SemanticallyValid(K) = StructuralValid(K) AND forall a: WellFormed(P(a)) [Q14, NEW]. EpistemicallyValid(K) = SemanticallyValid(K")

[different subject: assertion vs state; different arity: 4 vs 1; different nature: temporal+contextual applicability vs container integrity] They must never share the word Valid. (anchor: "Only StructuralValid and SemanticallyValid are computable from K alone. EpistemicallyValid requires evidence polarity; GovernanceValid requires History and is not a property of K.")
- [S1626] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Fully specifies concrete 11-field signatures for 12 named operations (create, assert, retract, relate, merge, supersede, refine, resolve, remove, replay, validate, assess), each rated computable=YES, directly executing the operation-registry schema Step 256 (S1623) had proposed abstractly -- e.g. retract has failure mode LOSSY-NO-INVERSE (executed), relate can fail via a cycle, merge may introduce contradiction (executed), replay is order-dependent (executed)." (anchor: "12 operations fully specified [create, assert, retract, relate, merge, supersede, refine, resolve, remove, replay, validate, assess] each with Input/Preconditions/Output/Postconditions/Det/Auth/Gov/Hist/Computable/Failure modes. All 12 rated Computable=YES.")
- [S1626] types=[DEFINITION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Classifies all acts into 4 kinds by a precise signature/effect table (transformation: mutates K, appends history; assessment: neither; decision: appends history without mutating K until subsequently asserted; governance action: appends history without mutating K), concluding validate and assess are the ONLY two operations that never change K -- they are queries wearing operation names, so any implementation where validation mutates state has conflated assessment with transformation, exactly the error Step 232.4 warns against." (anchor: "transformation: K x Op x Policy x Authority -> K [changes K: YES, appends History: YES]. assessment: P x Evidence x Context x Policy -> Sigma [changes K: no, appends History: no]. decision: Assessment x Authority -> Determination [changes K: no until asserted, appends History: YES]. governance actio")
- [S1626] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT, RESTATEMENT] scope=OBJECT — "Reconfirms and consolidates the executed algebraic laws first reported in S1617: (K,merge,empty) is a join-semilattice; assert is monotone; retract lacks a total inverse; split is lossy on R; merge preserves structural but not epistemic validity; replay is order-dependent; query is pure and monotone." (anchor: "(K, merge, empty) commutative associative idempotent identity empty => JOIN-SEMILATTICE. assert idempotent commutative associative MONOTONE. retract idempotent NOT monotone NO TOTAL INVERSE. split LOSSY on R. merge preserves StructuralValid, NOT EpistemicallyValid. replay deterministic ORDER-DEPENDE")
- [S1626] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Proves the (K,merge,empty) join-semilattice has no corresponding meet operation, since intersecting two knowledge states would discard assertions that no one explicitly retracted -- a deliberate, justified absence rather than an incompleteness, meaning K forms a join-semilattice but not a full lattice." (anchor: "merge is a join-semilattice but NOT a lattice -- no meet is defined, because intersecting two knowledge states is not a knowledge-preserving operation (it discards assertions no one retracted).
